content: Iloprost is indicated for the treatment of severe frostbite in adults to reduce the risk of digit amputation. It should be administered as a continuous intravenous infusion over six hours daily for up to a maximum of eight consecutive days. The dosage is determined based on the patient’s actual body weight. Its effectiveness has been demonstrated in young, healthy adults who experienced frostbite at high altitudes. Vital signs should be monitored before initiating treatment and with every dose adjustment. The safety and efficacy of iloprost have not been established in older adults (aged 65 years or older) due to insufficient representation in clinical studies. However, other clinical experiences with iloprost have not identified significant differences in responses between elderly and younger patients. When prescribing iloprost to older individuals, caution is advised. It is recommended to start at the lower end of the dosing range, considering the higher likelihood of reduced hepatic, renal, or cardiac function, as well as the presence of concurrent diseases or other drug therapies. Iloprost may interact with various medications, often leading to pharmacodynamic synergism, which can enhance the effects of either drug. In such cases, temporary discontinuation of the concomitant vasodilators or antihypertensive medications should be considered to mitigate these effects. Specific drug interactions include, but are not limited to, aldesleukin, alfentanil, alprostadil, amantadine, amifostine, amiodarone, amphotericin B (in various formulations), amyl nitrite, apomorphine, bortezomib, bretylium, bromocriptine, bupivacaine, chlorpromazine, clofarabine, clomipramine, clozapine, conivaptan, desflurane, dexmedetomidine, diltiazem, dinutuximab, enflurane, fenoldopam, fentanyl, ferric gluconate, foscarbidopa/foslevodopa, hydralazine, imipramine, iron sucrose, isocarboxazid, isoflurane, isosorbide dinitrate, isosorbide mononitrate, levodopa (including inhaled formulations), lofexidine, meperidine, minoxidil, morphine, nabilone, nadolol, nesiritide, nitric oxide gas, and various forms of nitroglycerin (IV, oral, sublingual, and topical).
